## 固定收益市場主論

8月31日，美國與伊朗再度交戰，紐約交易時段油價上揚，市場擔心能源成本使聯準會更難壓低通膨。美國公債自5年期到長天期全面走弱：10年期殖利率上升3.1個基點至4.751%，為2025年1月以來首次突破4.75%；30年期上升3.6個基點至5.243%。對政策較敏感的2年期殖利率則微降0.2個基點至4.343%，使殖利率曲線趨陡。前一交易日，聯準會主席Kevin Warsh在傑克森洞的演說引發的賣壓主要集中於短天期。

美軍攻擊荷莫茲海峽一座島嶼，伊朗攻擊阿拉伯聯合大公國與約旦，美國總統川普表示將作出回應，但未說明方式。紐約收盤時，WTI期貨上漲3.55%至每桶$86.36；布蘭特期貨雖曾在局勢升溫時盤中上漲，最終仍下跌0.81%至$88.59。WTI漲勢反映當天的能源風險，但兩項指標收盤走勢分歧，不足以判斷油價衝擊會否持續。

10年期實質殖利率上升2.8個基點至2.43%，幾乎占了名目殖利率的全部升幅；10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.3個基點至2.321%。投資人要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，才願意承擔長天期債券的利率風險，卻未大幅提高長期通膨補償。Warsh在9月是否升息仍不確定：交換市場反映的升息機率約為60%，數名債券經理人則懷疑聯準會是否會把他強硬的抗通膨措辭化為行動。長天期債券同時承受這項政策不確定性、潛在公司債供給及油價風險。

其他市場也有各自的壓力。印度成長意外強勁、德國通膨上升，支撐兩地的緊縮預期；日本10年期公債殖利率在標售前逼近3%。哥倫比亞政府提出約$110億的額外借款計畫，形成另一種融資衝擊。信用市場則呈現分歧：加州公用事業債券因野火賠償責任走弱；CDK以債權人讓步洽談延長到期日；瑞士國會議員推進一項提案，可能允許瑞銀以改革後的AT1債券滿足部分新增資本要求。

## 油價、政策疑慮與供給壓力推升美國長債殖利率

美國與伊朗約一個月來首次直接互相攻擊，使市場再次擔心荷莫茲海峽航運持續受阻。投資人同時評估，能源價格上漲會否妨礙通膨出現Warsh要求的改善。川普威脅進一步攻擊後，兩項原油指標在美國上午交易時段觸及當日高點；但收盤時只有WTI大幅上漲，布蘭特已回吐盤中漲幅。美國公債的反應較一致，中天期及長天期殖利率均上升。

海灣航運雖已脫離最嚴重的低谷，仍未恢復到戰前水準。高盛研究人員估計，近期海灣地區每日出口約1,500萬至1,600萬桶，比3月低點高出約500萬至600萬桶，但仍較戰前少700萬至800萬桶。估算也納入因油輪關閉應答器或在船舶間轉運貨物而較難追蹤的航次。新一輪攻擊使這部分復甦能否維持受到質疑。油價上漲可直接推高短期消費價格；若漲勢持續，也會使聯準會更難認定基礎通膨正以足夠速度趨近2%。

Warsh上週五已說明政策條件：近期較佳的通膨數據，尚不足以證明基礎趨勢有實質改善。巴克萊與法國興業銀行隨後把今年升息納入預測。SEI Investments的Sean Simko認為，若就業穩定而通膨維持高位，聯準會很可能在9月16日決議升息。因此，8月非農就業報告與9月11日消費者物價數據，比再次泛泛表達對通膨的憂慮更具決定性。

債市尚未對升息形成共識。TD Securities仍以按兵不動為基本情境。ABN AMRO Investment Solutions的Christophe Boucher認為，若通膨持續而9月再次不升息，市場可能重新質疑聯準會的公信力；DWS的George Catrambone則指出，零售銷售與就業尚未顯示經濟重新加速。Brandywine Global的Tracy Chen也希望實際政策行動能支持Warsh的措辭。這些分歧有助於解釋週一的殖利率走勢：2年期未延續上週五的急升，但投資人衡量能源衝擊與政策決定仍不明朗的代價，持續賣出長天期公債。

2年期與10年期利差擴大3.3個基點至40.8個基點，2年期與30年期利差擴大3.8個基點至90.0個基點。兩者仍窄於一週前，表示週一只逆轉了Warsh演說後曲線趨平走勢的一部分。5年期殖利率上升2.1個基點至4.501%，達2025年初以來最高；30年期殖利率則超越前一週高點。實質殖利率升幅遠大於損益兩平通膨率，也顯示市場反應不只是調高預期通膨。

月底需求未明顯緩解最長天期債券的賣壓。紐約時間下午4時指數調整時，納入債券基準指數的10年至30年期美國公債規模高於往常，30年期殖利率卻仍維持上升。期貨交易也激增：12月到期的10年期公債期貨在一分鐘內成交近24.4萬口，接近全天成交量的10%。另有一筆約花費$650萬的選擇權交易，尋求對沖長債下跌、30年期殖利率接近5.7%的情境；選擇權於11月20日到期。這些交易反映市場關注長天期進一步走弱的風險，但都不能預示殖利率最終走向。

預期9月將發行的公司債，也將占用投資人承接長天期債券的能力。Potomac River Capital的Mark Spindel指出，後續供給尤其是公司債發行，加上他認為改善有限的通膨前景，均構成壓力。美國財政部計畫將未償還10年至30年期公債的回購規模至少加倍，仍是相反方向的支撐：即使週一上升，30年期殖利率仍低於8月稍早觸及的多年高點。Brandywine在回購計畫宣布後，已縮減長天期美債的減碼幅度。

Stanley Druckenmiller主張政策制定者不應藉此干預債市定價，財政部長Scott Bessent週一則為擴大回購辯護。他表示，目的是減緩單邊交易、讓市場聚焦基本面，而非指定殖利率水準。他認為回購或許有助於美債在8月優於其他主要國家公債：當月美國10年期殖利率約上升2個基點，德國上升逾10個基點，日本約上升15個基點。但相對表現無法單獨證明回購的效果，週一走勢也顯示油價與政策風險仍能推升美債殖利率。

Bessent也延後了提出財政整頓方案的可能時間。他8月20日曾表示，或許會在8月底左右宣布；週一改稱，他與白宮預算主管Russ Vought將在未來數週或數月討論方案。投資人評估未來美債融資需求及秋季可能繁忙的公司債發行之際，財政計畫仍未明朗。

跨資產交易未呈現全面撤離風險的景象。標普500指數下跌0.33%至7,686.14點，納斯達克100指數上漲0.08%，半導體指數上漲0.57%；VIX上升3.40%至14.92。美元指數上漲0.26%至99.416，黃金期貨上漲0.44%至每盎司$4,498。債券基金方面，LQD與EMB各下跌0.13%，HYG與JNK則各上漲約0.09%。這些價格變動與美債顯著走弱並存，卻未顯示投資人一致撤出信用債或科技股。

## 印度、德國與日本面臨不同的緊縮考驗

在主要利率市場中，印度公布了最強勁的新成長數據。4月至6月一季GDP年增7.8%，高於預估中位數7.3%及印度央行預測的7%；前一季增幅也由7.8%上修至8.6%，為現行數據序列最高。這份報告緩解了油價衝擊與供應中斷已使印度內需停滯的疑慮。數據公布後印度公債仍維持跌勢，指標10年期殖利率上升4個基點至6.95%。

成長涵蓋多個領域，使數據更具政策分量。製造業成長由8.3%加快至9.2%，金融服務業由8.8%加快至12.1%；固定資本形成總額增幅由5.8%升至11.9%，民間消費則由6.8%升至7.1%。生產、投資與家庭支出同步擴張，難以歸因於單一產業。若通膨壓力持續，印度央行也較難以成長疲弱為由暫緩升息。

印度央行8月將政策利率維持在5.25%，並表示若價格壓力累積，可能需要升息。Kotak Mahindra Bank首席經濟學家Upasna Bhardwaj預期，本財年下半年將升息50個基點，理由是成長強勁、通膨偏高，且扣除通膨後的利率下降。首席經濟顧問V. Anantha Nageswaran提出較審慎的官方判斷：通膨仍在央行2%至6%的容忍區間內，決策者正觀察第二輪價格效應，再決定是否行動。利率決策委員會將於10月5日至7日再次開會。

印度近90%的原油仰賴進口，因此荷莫茲海峽周邊若持續受阻，可能推高通膨、削弱家庭購買力並擠壓企業利潤。GDP顯示最近一季的經濟仍具韌性，卻無法判斷若油價長期上漲，消費者與企業能承受多大漲幅，而不引發更廣泛的價格效應。

德國8月通膨則向歐洲央行提供了更直接的價格訊號。消費者物價年增率由2.8%升至2.9%，為4月以來最高，但低於預估中位數3.1%。6月臨時燃油減負措施到期後，暖氣用油及加油成本上升，帶動能源價格；服務與食品通膨卻放緩。決策者判斷外來價格衝擊是否擴散至國內物價時，後兩項變化是重要限制。

歐洲央行已升息一次，市場預期9月10日會再次行動。目前存款利率為2.25%，被視為既不刺激也不抑制需求的水準；官員則討論政策是否需要轉為略具限制性。斯洛維尼亞籍管委Primoz Dolenc上週表示，9月升息已有其理由。奧地利籍管委Martin Kocher認為，目前尚無第二輪效應的明確證據，秋季數據對後續利率路徑將十分重要。德國通膨支持近期升息，但低於預期的整體數值及放緩的服務通膨，使之後需要緊縮到什麼程度仍未明朗。

日本債市在下次政策會議前，已反映相當大的利率調整。10年期公債殖利率週一盤中觸及2.95%，為1996年以來最高，逼近3%。上週2年期標售疲弱之後，投資人將面對週二的10年期標售；前次10年期標售投標倍數為2.56，創2025年5月以來最低。法國巴黎資產管理策略師Ryutaro Kimura認為，市場在日本央行開會前觀望，可能削弱投標需求；但接近3%的殖利率也可能吸引部分買家，限制進一步升幅。

日圓疲弱是同一政策環境的另一面。7月下旬啟動干預行動後取得的升值幅度，已有逾半數回吐，匯價一度貶破160日圓兌1美元。日本財務省表示，之前一個月動用創紀錄的¥15.4兆，即$964億；美國也在7月31日參與買入日圓的行動。日圓由上週五收盤的160.09，回升至週一紐約下午的159.69。策略師認為，161及其後的162至163區間可能提高干預風險；日本官員則強調匯價變動的速度及是否失序，而非固定匯率門檻。選擇權定價顯示，市場對日圓升值保護的需求低於8月初極端時的水準。

Bessent也加大了要求日本作出貨幣政策回應的壓力。據週日報導，他認為日本可能已走到安倍經濟學相關再通膨政策的終點，但不會指示日本央行如何行動。週一他表示，相信日本政府與央行將採取使日圓走強的措施。NHK其後引述美國財政部國際事務次長Erin Browne報導，Bessent曾告訴財務大臣片山皋月與日本央行總裁植田和男，日本下一步應升息，並清楚說明如何邁向可持續的公共財政。這項轉述比他先前的公開說法更明確；政策決定仍由日本央行作出。

日本殖利率上升，也引發擴大國內買盤的討論。分析師認為，日本年金積立金管理運用獨立行政法人GPIF可能考慮調高目前25%的日本債券目標配置。GPIF管理約¥318兆資產，配置比例每增加1個百分點，帳面上相當於逾¥3兆的配置變動。第一生命經濟研究所的Koji Okuda建議，先評估不同經濟情境下的報酬與風險，再研究將目標提高至30%至35%。野村估計，一般再平衡已使GPIF在4月至6月買入¥5.7兆日本公債，為至少2020財年以來最大季度買入量。

正式調整目標配置則是另一項決策。Okuda估計，若日本債券配置提高至30%、同時減少外國債券，須買入約¥16兆日圓；目標若升至35%，金額將達¥32兆。GPIF表示，目前投資環境與其現行投資組合所依據的假設並無重大差異。其他分析師提醒，增加國內債券比重，可能需要在其他資產承擔更多風險才能達成報酬目標；名目殖利率上升，考慮薪資成長後也未必意味同樣具吸引力的報酬。眼前更直接的考驗，是殖利率接近3%時標售能否順利完成，而非退休基金會否調整長期配置。

## 哥倫比亞增債計畫考驗新興市場需求

哥倫比亞政府把龐大的財政缺口，轉化為眼前的融資問題。據與會人士透露，公共信貸主管Cesar Arias告訴造市商，政府計畫今年額外籌措約$110億，並以債務交換管理2026年的融資需求。其中逾$30億預計來自外部借款，主要透過發債；本地則擬籌集約25兆哥倫比亞披索。財政部未立即對此說法置評。

政府先前公布2027年初步赤字將達GDP的9.4%，已引發賣壓：哥倫比亞本幣10年期公債殖利率當時跳升逾30個基點，披索最多貶值2.1%。新增融資計畫公布後，本地殖利率與交換利率週一再度上升，披索下跌0.9%，為當天表現最弱的新興市場貨幣。相較於市場已知的赤字數字，新資訊是今年額外借款的規模及擬議籌資方式。

BTG Pactual分析師認為，這項計畫將對本地債券形成顯著供給衝擊，殖利率曲線中段及長端預計承受大部分調整。近期要看標售是否須提供更大的殖利率讓步，或是否出現需求減弱，尤其是較長天期債券。今年哥倫比亞本地債券已上漲29%，在彭博指數的新興市場同業中表現最佳；高殖利率、匯價升值，以及市場對總統Abelardo de la Espriella的樂觀情緒，曾支持這波漲勢，也使價格容易受到融資前景惡化的衝擊。

政府或可減少直接交由債券投資人承接的規模，但仍須實際取得其他資金。XP Investments的Andres Pardo預期政府將尋求多邊機構融資。財政部長Miguel Gómez預定在9月7日當週訪問紐約與華盛頓，並已表示哥倫比亞並非尋求國際貨幣基金紓困。T. Rowe Price分析師Christopher Mejía認為，若政府落實財政整頓立法，並利用多邊機構及其他來源減輕債券供給，增加借款仍可能可控。Bancolombia執行長Juan Carlos Mora則表示，投資人會仔細檢視資金實際來自何處。

哥倫比亞的變化，與市場對本幣計價新興市場債券的整體興趣形成對照。依彭博總報酬指數，這類債券今年報酬率達3.3%，已開發市場同業則為負1.9%；即使3月美伊戰爭爆發時，新興市場債券曾下跌3.8%，全年表現仍較佳。摩根大通資產管理、景順及Marlborough Investment Management的經理人認為，若干開發中經濟體控制通膨、維持財政紀律，加上投資人希望分散美元資產，均增添吸引力。但哥倫比亞的融資衝擊說明，整體市場的投資理由無法取代對個別國家資金需求的計算。美國殖利率升高與油價再度上漲的壓力，也帶來不同挑戰，對能源進口國尤其如此。

智利企業信用風險的前景較有利，但仍有財政上的限制。在24名分析師與交易員的調查中，17%表示9月願意買入評級低至BBB的智利公司債，占比逾上月3倍，為3月以來最高。態度轉變出現在總統José Antonio Kast經濟法案的核心內容獲批准之後；法案包括降低企業稅及減少繁瑣規定，財政部長Jorge Quiroz表示將於9月上半月生效。智利預算機關預測明年經濟成長3.7%，經濟部則表示，1月至7月新設企業達創紀錄的140,412家。

預期中的改善尚未反映於產出：智利經濟第1季萎縮0.3%後，第2季持平。改革預計也會使政府收入至少減少五年，總債務逼近部分分析師認為可能引發評級下調風險的GDP 45%水準。因此，調查呈現的是市場因期待投資復甦而更願意承擔企業信用風險；主權財政則可能負擔推動復甦的部分成本。

## 債權條件與放款能力受到更嚴格檢視

加州議員未納入州長Gavin Newsom要求的一項主要保障，公用事業債券因而走弱。州長提議禁止保險公司透過代位求償，向公用事業公司追討野火損失；週六提出的法案雖將調整州內野火制度，卻保留這條求償途徑。截至週一紐約時間上午8時43分，PG&E票息6.3%、2056年到期債券的利差擴大15個基點至138個基點；Edison International票息4%、2047年到期票據的利差擴大10個基點至133個基點。

Impax Asset Management的Tony Trzcinka認為，刪去這項保障對公用事業信用狀況有實質負面影響，若出現評級下調也不令人意外。議員擔心取消代位求償會提高家庭保費，因此改提禁止保險公司將對公用事業的求償權出售給避險基金等投資人，並限制特別嚴重野火發生後的主管獎金、加快向受災者付款及加強預防措施。這些規定改變索賠處理與誘因，公用事業公司仍須承擔保險公司日後求償的風險。議員可能於週二表決。

汽車經銷商軟體供應商CDK Global的方案，則重新分配不同債權人的風險。據知情人士透露，CDK已與貸款人指導委員會達成框架：公司所有者Brookfield Business Partners將把所持約$6.75億債權，換成受償順位較低、以債付息（PIK）的債務。所有者的債權順位下移，將改善參與方案的有擔保貸款人相對順位；以新增債務支付利息，則可保留CDK現金。

作為交換，指導委員會的貸款人將以8%折價，把2029年到期的有擔保債務換成到期日延後2.5年的債務。若Brookfield在交易完成前持續於次級市場回購債務，最高可取得13%折價，回購上限約$12億。CDK近$40億的2029年到期定期貸款，上週五交易價格為面額每$1對應$0.52。獲利疲弱、高槓桿及2024年網路攻擊的後續影響，使延長到期日具有價值，也解釋了債權人為何被要求接受價格讓步。

貸款人的合作協議禁止委員會成員退出並單獨談判。知情人士表示，CDK接下來將與其餘貸款人洽談，給予他們的條件不得優於委員會。穆迪8月初以營收低迷、槓桿及再融資風險為由，將CDK評級下調2級至Caa2。擬議換債將改變受償順位及還款時點；債權人的最終回收價值，仍取決於延後到期之前營運能否改善。

瑞士上議院委員會以10票贊成、2票反對、1票棄權，建議允許瑞銀以改革後的其他第一類資本債券（AT1），滿足擬議新增資本要求的最高50%。政府要求瑞銀增資約$200億，以保護瑞士實體免受海外子公司虧損波及。若可用部分AT1取代普通股，瑞銀的融資成本可能降低。瑞銀現有AT1約占歐洲$2,860億市場的7%，使提案的影響不限於單一銀行。

委員會將這項彈性與更早吸收損失的機制綁定。依擬議規定，若瑞銀普通股權益資本低於最低要求，就須停止發放股利、股票回購及AT1票息，並縮減獎金總額。財政部質疑AT1在危機時能否像普通股一樣可靠地吸收損失。社會民主黨批評委員會決定，下議院也可能推翻這些讓步。上議院預計在9月14日至10月2日會期進行下一次表決；立法程序至少將延續至明年。

亞洲資料中心融資則面臨銀行放款能力的限制。自2025年初以來，該產業貸款已接近$290億，其中今年迄今達創紀錄的$150億，比2025年同期高27%。總部位於新加坡的DayOne Data Centers正洽談將既有貸款額度擴大至最高$70億；若成案，將是亞洲規模最大的資料中心債務融資。巴克萊的Andrew Ashman表示，對該產業曝險較高的銀行愈來愈挑剔，偏好熟悉的借款人或報酬較高的交易。

部分貸款人也試圖分散既有曝險。法國農業信貸銀行尋求出售一筆香港資料中心貸款的部分權益，摩根士丹利則研究以重大風險轉移交易對沖部位。巴克萊的Richard Satchwell認為，資產擔保證券及專案債券可讓較長期資本市場承接部分融資，協助銀行騰出資本再放款；同時，債券投資人也將承接更多專案興建及營運風險。輝達宣布透過可轉換債券投資台灣聯發科$35億，為其在美國境外最大的直接投資，顯示策略性科技資金仍在流動，儘管為實體設施融資的銀行已表示承作空間趨緊。

## 後續市場觀察

接下來的美國數據，將檢驗經濟活動與通膨是否支持週一長天期公債的跌勢。9月1日紐約時間上午9時45分，標普全球將公布製造業指數終值，市場共識為53.2，前值53.9；上午10時公布的ISM製造業指數，共識為55.2，前值55.6。ISM的訂單、就業及價格分項須合併觀察：若生產維持韌性、投入成本又走強，將支持能源壓力正作用於仍有能力承受的經濟這一判斷。

7月JOLTS職位空缺及營建支出也在上午10時公布。職位空缺預計由735.9萬降至730萬，將在週五非農就業報告前提供勞動需求廣度的最新訊息；營建支出預計在前值下降0.1%後持平，可供觀察高借貸成本下的需求。經濟學家預期8月非農就業增加5.5萬人，7月則意外減少，失業率預計維持4.1%。若結果接近預測，聯準會對通膨的評估仍是核心；若就業明顯較弱，9月繼續按兵不動將更容易獲得支持。

9月11日的消費者物價數據，將更直接檢驗Warsh在聯準會9月16日開會前，要求看到通膨更明確趨近2%的條件。對債券而言，問題是9月決定會否確認短天期殖利率已反映的緊縮預期；若不升息，長天期投資人則仍須評估央行公信力與通膨風險。荷莫茲海峽相關油價走勢同樣重要，因為數據公布之間若能源價格再次持續上漲，物價前景可能改變。

日本10年期公債標售結果預定週二東京時間中午12時35分公布。以殖利率接近3%時的投標需求，對照前次標售2.56的投標倍數，可判斷日本央行9月17日至18日開會前，國內買家是否願意承接利率風險。週四的30年期標售則將另行檢驗超長天期需求。德國通膨各分項的變化，使市場聚焦歐洲央行9月10日決議，以及之後薪資或服務價格是否出現傳導的證據。受訪的21名經濟學家全數預期紐西蘭央行週三將把官方現金利率上調25個基點至2.75%；在通膨已達4.1%、失業率也升至5.6%的情況下，聲明將影響市場對後續升息速度的判斷。

融資決策提供比整體風險偏好更具體的觀察點。哥倫比亞後續標售將顯示，增加本地債券供給需要多少殖利率讓步；Gómez在9月7日當週的會晤，可能釐清債券與多邊機構資金各占多少。加州議員週二的表決，將決定PG&E及Edison面對的野火賠償責任條款。CDK須按已議定的受償順位條件，爭取其餘貸款人參與換債；瑞銀的AT1折衷方案能否推進，則取決於秋季國會表決。DayOne最終的融資規模、定價及貸款人參與情況，將顯示亞洲銀行還能承作或分散多少資料中心曝險。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場數值均以紐約收盤為基準。利率資料採用彭博每日殖利率歷史序列；變動幅度與推算的殖利率曲線使用相同日期的序列。每日歷史資料未標明具體觀察時間。

overall_summary.headline: 美伊再度交戰引發通膨疑慮，美國長天期公債殖利率上升
overall_summary.session_narrative:
8月31日，美國與伊朗再度互相攻擊，市場擔心能源成本使聯準會更難壓低通膨，美國公債自5年期到長天期走弱。10年期殖利率上升3.1個基點至4.751%，為2025年1月以來首次突破4.75%；30年期升至5.243%。2年期殖利率微降，使曲線趨陡；前一交易日，聯準會主席Kevin Warsh的演說則曾引發短天期賣壓。10年期實質殖利率幾乎占了名目殖利率全部升幅，預期中的公司債供給也對長天期債券形成壓力。

WTI上漲3.55%至每桶$86.36，但布蘭特盤中上漲後收低0.81%；兩者收盤走勢不足以判斷油價衝擊會否持續。投資人對Warsh是否會在9月升息仍有分歧。其他市場方面，印度成長強勁、德國通膨上升，支撐當地緊縮預期；日本10年期殖利率在標售前逼近3%，哥倫比亞則提出約$110億的額外借款計畫。
overall_summary.summary: 荷莫茲海峽附近再度交戰推高WTI，美國10年期公債殖利率突破4.75%；2年期殖利率微降，長天期殖利率升幅則主要來自實質殖利率。

section_summaries.summary: 美國長天期公債殖利率上升、2年期微降，使曲線趨陡，部分逆轉前一交易日由短天期主導的走勢。荷莫茲海峽周邊再度交戰引發能源疑慮，但WTI上漲、布蘭特收低，對持續性油價衝擊發出不同訊號。Warsh在9月的利率決定及潛在公司債供給，也對長天期債券形成壓力。

section_summaries.market_read: 實質殖利率而非損益兩平通膨率顯著上升，顯示投資人要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，才願意持有承受利率風險的債券。
section_summaries.section_title: 油價、政策疑慮與供給壓力推升美國長債殖利率
section_summaries.summary: 美伊新一輪攻擊使海灣出口能否維持部分復甦受到質疑。Warsh認為近期通膨數據尚未顯示基礎趨勢充分改善，但債券經理人對聯準會9月會否升息意見分歧。投資人同時衡量油價、政策不確定性與即將到來的公司債發行，賣出長天期美債；財政部擴大回購仍可能提供需求。

section_summaries.section_title: 印度、德國與日本面臨不同的緊縮考驗
section_summaries.summary: 印度GDP年增7.8%，優於預期；若通膨持續，印度央行較難以成長疲弱為由暫緩升息。德國通膨升至2.9%，支持歐洲央行近期緊縮，但服務通膨放緩，使後續幅度仍未明朗。日本10年期公債殖利率在標售前一度達2.95%；日圓疲弱增添政策壓力，GPIF提高國內債券配置目前仍只是可能性。

section_summaries.section_title: 哥倫比亞增債計畫考驗新興市場需求
section_summaries.summary: 哥倫比亞計畫今年額外籌措約$110億，延續先前公布2027年初步赤字後的債券及披索跌勢。後續標售將檢驗投資人要求多少殖利率讓步；若取得多邊機構資金，直接發債規模可望減少。智利經濟改革取得進展後，市場更願意買入評級較低的公司債，但產出疲弱及改革的財政成本仍限制前景。

美國製造業數據、非農就業及9月11日消費者物價，將在聯準會9月16日決議前，檢驗經濟活動與通膨是否支持長天期美債跌勢。日本10年期標售將衡量殖利率接近3%時的需求；哥倫比亞標售及融資會晤，則將釐清多少借款須由債券投資人承接。歐洲央行與日本央行決議、債權人相關表決及資料中心融資條件，也將提供後續觀察依據。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off from the 5-year sector through the long end on Aug. 31 as renewed US-Iran fighting lifted oil during New York trading and sharpened concern that energy costs would complicate the Federal Reserve’s inflation fight. The 10-year yield rose 3.1 basis points to 4.751%, crossing 4.75% for the first time since January 2025. The 30-year yield added 3.6 basis points to 5.243%, while the policy-sensitive 2-year edged 0.2 basis point lower to 4.343%. The result was a steeper curve, one session after Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech had concentrated the selloff at shorter maturities.

American forces struck an island in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran attacked the United Arab Emirates and Jordan, and President Donald Trump said the US would respond without specifying how. WTI futures gained 3.55% to $86.36 at the New York close. Brent futures, despite an intraday rise reported as tensions escalated, finished 0.81% lower at $88.59. The split between the benchmarks does not erase the day’s energy scare, but it narrows what their closing prices say about a sustained oil shock.

The 10-year real yield rose 2.8 basis points to 2.43%, accounting for almost all the nominal yield increase; the 10-year breakeven rose just 0.3 basis point to 2.321%. Investors demanded more inflation-adjusted return to hold duration without marking up longer-term inflation compensation much. Warsh’s September rate decision remained uncertain: swaps pricing put the chance of an increase at roughly 60%, while several bond managers questioned whether the Fed would follow his firm inflation language with action. The longer end had to absorb that uncertainty alongside prospective corporate supply and the oil risk.

Elsewhere, India’s unexpectedly strong growth and Germany’s higher inflation supported local tightening expectations, while Japan’s 10-year yield neared 3% ahead of an auction. Colombia faced a distinct financing shock after its government outlined about $11 billion of additional borrowing. Corporate credit was similarly selective: California utilities lost ground on wildfire liability, CDK negotiated a maturity extension with creditor concessions, and Swiss lawmakers advanced a proposal that could let UBS meet part of a new capital requirement with reformed AT1 debt.

## Oil, Policy Doubts and Supply Lift Longer Treasury Yields

The US-Iran exchange was the first direct round of attacks in about a month. The renewed fighting revived concern that traffic through the Strait of Hormuz would remain disrupted, just as investors were assessing whether higher energy prices could prevent the inflation improvement Warsh says he needs to see. Oil benchmarks reached session highs during the US morning after Trump threatened further attacks. In the completed close, WTI rose sharply while Brent gave back its earlier gain; the Treasury response was clearer, with yields rising across intermediate and long maturities.

Shipping had improved from its worst point without returning to prewar conditions. Goldman Sachs researchers estimated recent Gulf exports at roughly 15 million to 16 million barrels a day, about 5 million to 6 million above the March low but still 7 million to 8 million below prewar levels. Their estimate includes voyages made harder to track because tankers have turned off transponders or transferred cargo between ships. The new attacks put the durability of that partial recovery in question. Higher oil can affect near-term consumer prices directly and, if it persists, make it harder for the Fed to conclude that underlying inflation is moving toward 2% quickly enough.

Warsh had supplied the policy condition on Friday, saying better recent inflation readings did not yet amount to meaningful improvement in the underlying trend. Barclays and Société Générale subsequently moved to forecasts that included rate increases this year. Sean Simko of SEI Investments said steady employment alongside elevated inflation would probably push the Fed toward an increase at its Sept. 16 decision. The August payroll report and Sept. 11 consumer-price release are therefore more consequential than another general expression of concern about inflation.

The bond market has not settled on that outcome. TD Securities retained a hold as its base case. Christophe Boucher of ABN AMRO Investment Solutions said another September hold with persistent inflation could revive doubts about the Fed’s credibility, while George Catrambone of DWS argued that retail sales and employment have not signaled renewed economic acceleration. Brandywine Global’s Tracy Chen also wanted action to substantiate Warsh’s language. Their disagreement helps explain the shape of Monday’s move: the 2-year yield did not extend Friday’s sharp rise, but longer bonds sold off as investors weighed both an energy shock and the cost of another uncertain policy decision.

The 2s10s spread widened 3.3 basis points to 40.8 basis points, and 2s30s widened 3.8 basis points to 90.0. Both remained narrower than a week earlier, so Monday reversed only part of the flattening associated with Warsh’s speech. Five-year yields rose 2.1 basis points to 4.501%, reaching their highest level since early 2025, while 30-year yields exceeded the previous week’s highs. The rise in real yields rather than breakevens shows that the market’s response extended beyond a simple increase in expected inflation.

Month-end demand offered little visible relief to the longest maturities. At the 4 p.m. New York index rebalance, a larger-than-usual volume of 10- to 30-year Treasury debt entered bond benchmarks, yet the 30-year yield stayed higher. Futures activity surged: nearly 244,000 December 10-year note contracts traded in one minute, close to 10% of the day’s volume. Separately, an options purchase costing about $6.5 million sought protection against a long-bond decline consistent with a 30-year yield near 5.7%; those options expire Nov. 20. The trades show attention to further long-end risk, though neither establishes where yields will go.

September’s expected corporate-bond calendar adds a prospective claim on investors’ capacity to absorb duration. Mark Spindel of Potomac River Capital cited forthcoming supply, especially corporate issuance, together with an inflation outlook he judged little improved. Treasury’s plan to at least double buybacks of outstanding 10- to 30-year debt remains a counterweight: the 30-year yield, despite Monday’s rise, stayed below the multiyear highs reached earlier in August. Brandywine had reduced its underweight in long Treasuries after that announcement.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the buyback expansion on Monday after Stanley Druckenmiller argued that policymakers should let the bond market set prices without such intervention. Bessent said he wanted to slow one-way trading and keep attention on fundamentals, rather than dictate yields. He suggested the operation might have helped Treasuries outperform other major sovereign bonds in August: the US 10-year yield rose about 2 basis points over the month, compared with more than 10 basis points in Germany and about 15 in Japan. That relative result does not isolate the effect of buybacks, and Monday showed that oil and policy risk could still raise US yields.

Bessent also moved back the likely timing of a fiscal-consolidation presentation. After indicating on Aug. 20 that an announcement might come around the end of August, he said Monday that he and White House budget director Russ Vought would discuss a package in the coming weeks or months. The delay leaves the fiscal plan unresolved while investors assess future Treasury financing and a potentially heavy autumn corporate calendar.

Cross-asset trading offered a more mixed picture than a broad retreat from risk. The S&P 500 fell 0.33% to 7,686.14, but the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.08% and the semiconductor index rose 0.57%. The VIX increased 3.40% to 14.92. The US Dollar Index rose 0.26% to 99.416 and gold futures gained 0.44% to $4,498. In bond funds, LQD fell 0.13% and EMB lost 0.13%, while HYG and JNK each gained about 0.09%. Those price moves sit alongside a substantial Treasury selloff without establishing a uniform withdrawal from credit or technology risk.

## India, Germany and Japan Face Different Tightening Tests

India delivered the strongest fresh growth reading among the major rate markets. Gross domestic product expanded 7.8% from a year earlier in the April-June quarter, beating the 7.3% median estimate and the Reserve Bank of India’s 7% forecast. Growth in the preceding quarter was revised to 8.6% from 7.8%, the highest reading in the current data series. The report reduced concern that the oil shock and supply disruption had already stalled domestic demand, and Indian bonds retained losses after its release: the benchmark 10-year yield was up 4 basis points at 6.95%.

The breadth of the expansion gave it policy weight. Manufacturing grew 9.2%, up from 8.3%, while financial services increased 12.1% after 8.8%. Gross fixed-capital formation accelerated to 11.9% from 5.8%, and private consumption rose 7.1% versus 6.8% previously. The combination of production, investment and household spending is harder to dismiss as a single-sector gain. It also leaves less evidence of a growth constraint on the RBI if inflation pressure persists.

The RBI held its benchmark rate at 5.25% in August and has signaled that an increase may be needed if prices build. Upasna Bhardwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, expects 50 basis points of tightening in the second half of the fiscal year, citing strong growth, elevated inflation and falling inflation-adjusted rates. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran offered a narrower official assessment: inflation remains within the RBI’s 2%-6% tolerance band, he said, and policymakers are watching for second-round effects before deciding whether to act. The committee next reviews rates on Oct. 5-7.

India’s energy exposure keeps that distinction consequential. It imports nearly 90% of its crude, making sustained disruption around Hormuz a potential source of higher inflation, weaker household purchasing power and pressure on company margins. The GDP figures show resilience through the latest quarter; they do not settle how much of a prolonged oil increase consumers and firms can absorb without broader price effects.

Germany’s August inflation report gave the European Central Bank a more direct price signal. Consumer prices rose 2.9% from a year earlier, up from 2.8% and the strongest reading since April, although below the 3.1% median estimate. Energy drove the increase as heating-oil and pump costs rose after temporary fuel relief expired in June. Services and food inflation eased, an important qualification for officials deciding whether the imported shock is spreading into domestic prices.

The ECB has already raised borrowing costs once and is expected to act again on Sept. 10. Its deposit rate stands at 2.25%, a level described as neither stimulating nor constraining demand, while officials have discussed whether policy may need to become mildly restrictive. Slovenian Governing Council member Primoz Dolenc said last week that the arguments for a September increase were present. Austrian member Martin Kocher said there was no clear evidence yet of second-round effects and that autumn data would be important for the subsequent rate path. German inflation supports the near-term case, while its below-forecast reading and easing services component leave the depth of any later tightening open.

Japan’s bond market was already pricing a substantial adjustment before its next policy meeting. The 10-year government-bond yield briefly reached 2.95% on Monday, its highest since 1996 and close to 3%. Investors face Tuesday’s 10-year auction after a weak 2-year sale the previous week. The previous 10-year auction drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.56, its weakest since May 2025. BNP Paribas Asset Management strategist Ryutaro Kimura said a wait-and-see stance ahead of the Bank of Japan meeting could weaken demand, although some buyers may find a yield near 3% attractive enough to limit further increases.

Currency pressure is part of the same policy setting. The yen breached 160 per dollar after surrendering more than half the appreciation achieved during the intervention campaign that began in late July. Japan’s Finance Ministry reported spending a record ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, over the preceding month; the US also joined a yen-buying operation on July 31. The currency recovered from Friday’s 160.09 close to 159.69 by Monday afternoon in New York. Strategists identified 161 and then the 162-163 region as areas where intervention risk might rise, while Japanese officials have emphasized the speed and disorderliness of a move over any fixed exchange-rate threshold. Options pricing showed less demand for yen-upside protection than at its early-August extreme.

Bessent increased the pressure for a monetary response. In remarks reported Sunday, he said Japan had probably reached the end of the reflationary policy associated with Abenomics, though he would not tell the BOJ what to do. On Monday he said he believed Japan’s government and central bank would take steps leading to a stronger yen. NHK subsequently reported, citing Treasury Under Secretary for International Affairs Erin Browne, that Bessent told Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda that higher rates should be Japan’s next step and that they should make the path toward sustainable public finances clear. That account is more explicit than his earlier public formulation; the BOJ’s decision remains its own.

Higher Japanese yields are also prompting discussion about a larger domestic buyer base. Analysts said the Government Pension Investment Fund could consider raising its 25% target allocation to Japanese bonds. GPIF manages about ¥318 trillion, so a 1-percentage-point allocation change represents more than ¥3 trillion on paper. Koji Okuda of Daiichi Life Research Institute suggested examining a 30%-35% target after assessing returns and risk under different economic scenarios. Nomura estimated that ordinary rebalancing had already brought ¥5.7 trillion of JGB purchases in April-June, the largest quarterly amount since at least fiscal 2020.

A formal target change would be a different decision. Okuda estimated that moving domestic bonds to 30% while reducing foreign debt would entail about ¥16 trillion of yen buying, rising to ¥32 trillion at a 35% target. GPIF said it did not see the investment environment as materially different from the one assumed in its current portfolio. Other analysts warned that a higher domestic-bond weight could require more risk elsewhere to meet return goals, and that rising nominal yields do not necessarily mean equally attractive returns after wage growth is considered. The immediate test remains whether auctions clear at yields near 3%, before any change in the pension fund’s strategic allocation.

## Colombia’s Borrowing Plan Tests Emerging-Market Demand

Colombia’s government turned a large fiscal shortfall into an immediate financing question. Public credit director Cesar Arias told market makers that the administration planned to raise about $11 billion in additional financing this year and use debt swaps to manage its 2026 needs, according to people at the meeting. More than $3 billion is expected to come from external borrowing, mainly bond sales, and about 25 trillion pesos would be raised locally. The Finance Ministry did not immediately comment on the account.

The plan extended a selloff that began after the administration disclosed a preliminary 2027 deficit of 9.4% of GDP. Following that earlier announcement, Colombia’s 10-year local yield jumped more than 30 basis points and the peso weakened as much as 2.1%. Local yields and swap rates advanced again Monday; the peso fell 0.9%, the weakest performance among emerging-market currencies that day. The current change is the scale and proposed placement of this year’s additional borrowing, beyond the deficit number investors had already seen.

BTG Pactual analysts called the plan a significant supply shock for local bonds and expect the belly and long end of the curve to bear much of the adjustment. Their early test is whether coming auctions require larger yield concessions or draw weaker demand, especially for longer maturities. The concern is sharpened by Colombia’s previous performance: local bonds have returned 29% this year, the strongest result among emerging-market peers in a Bloomberg index. High yields, currency gains and optimism around President Abelardo de la Espriella had supported that advance, leaving prices sensitive to a worse financing outlook.

There is a possible way to limit the amount placed directly with bond investors, but it depends on execution. Andres Pardo of XP Investments expects the government to seek multilateral funding. Finance Minister Miguel Gómez is due to visit New York and Washington in the week of Sept. 7 and has said Colombia is not seeking an International Monetary Fund rescue. T. Rowe Price analyst Christopher Mejía said the larger borrowing could be manageable if the government follows through with fiscal-consolidation legislation and uses multilaterals and other sources to ease bond supply. Bancolombia Chief Executive Juan Carlos Mora said investors would scrutinize where the funding actually comes from.

The Colombian move stood out against broader interest in local-currency emerging-market debt. Such bonds have gained 3.3% this year, compared with a 1.9% decline for developed-market peers, according to Bloomberg total-return indexes, even after a 3.8% emerging-market fall when the US-Iran war began in March. Managers at JPMorgan Asset Management, Invesco and Marlborough Investment Management attributed part of the appeal to inflation control and fiscal discipline in several developing economies, alongside demand to diversify from dollar assets. Colombia’s funding shock shows why that aggregate case cannot substitute for a country’s financing arithmetic. A higher US yield and renewed oil pressure add separate challenges, particularly for energy importers.

Chile presented a more favorable corporate-risk outlook with a fiscal qualification. In a survey of 24 analysts and traders, 17% said they were willing to buy Chilean corporate debt rated as low as BBB for September, more than triple the previous month’s share and the highest since March. The shift followed approval of the core of President José Antonio Kast’s economic bill, which includes lower corporate taxes and less red tape; Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said it would be enacted in the first half of September. Chile’s budget office forecasts 3.7% growth next year, and the Economy Ministry reported a record 140,412 new companies registered in January-July.

The prospective improvement has yet to appear in output: Chile stagnated in Q2 after contracting 0.3% in Q1. The reform is also expected to reduce government revenue for at least five years, with gross debt approaching the 45%-of-GDP level that some analysts associate with downgrade risk. The survey therefore describes greater willingness to take corporate credit risk on an investment revival, while the sovereign may bear part of the cost of pursuing it.

## Creditor Terms and Lending Capacity Draw Closer Scrutiny

California utility bonds weakened after lawmakers omitted a central protection sought by Governor Gavin Newsom. His proposal would have barred insurers from seeking reimbursement from utilities for wildfire losses through subrogation. A bill introduced Saturday would change the state’s wildfire framework but leave that liability route in place. As of 8:43 a.m. Monday in New York, the spread on PG&E’s 6.3% bonds due in 2056 had widened 15 basis points to 138 basis points; Edison International’s 4% notes due in 2047 widened 10 basis points to 133.

Tony Trzcinka of Impax Asset Management called the omission materially negative for utility credit and said downgrades would not be surprising. Lawmakers were concerned that eliminating subrogation could raise household insurance premiums. Their bill would instead bar insurers from selling claims against utilities to investors such as hedge funds, restrict executive bonuses after particularly severe fires, speed payments to survivors and strengthen prevention efforts. Those changes affect claims handling and incentives, while utilities remain exposed to future insurer claims. Lawmakers are likely to vote Tuesday.

CDK Global’s creditors faced a different allocation of risk. The car-dealership software provider reached a framework with a lender steering committee under which owner Brookfield Business Partners would exchange about $675 million of its holdings for lower-ranking debt that pays interest in kind, according to people familiar with the talks. Subordinating the sponsor’s claim would improve the participating secured lenders’ relative position; paying interest with additional debt would conserve CDK’s cash.

In exchange, steering-committee lenders would swap secured debt due in 2029 for obligations maturing 2.5 years later at an 8% discount. Brookfield could obtain a discount of as much as 13% if it keeps repurchasing debt in the secondary market before the deal closes, with purchases capped at about $1.2 billion. CDK’s nearly $4 billion 2029 term loan traded at 52 cents on Friday. Weak earnings, high leverage and the lingering effects of a 2024 cyberattack make the maturity extension valuable, but also explain the price concessions creditors are being asked to make.

The lenders’ cooperation agreement prevents committee members from breaking away to negotiate separately. CDK will seek terms with remaining lenders, whose treatment cannot be better than the committee’s, the people said. Moody’s cut the company 2 notches to Caa2 in early August, citing muted revenue, leverage and refinancing risk. The proposed exchange changes priority and timing; its eventual value to creditors still depends on whether operations improve before the extended debt matures.

In Switzerland, an upper-house committee voted 10-2, with one abstention, to recommend that reformed Additional Tier 1 debt cover as much as 50% of UBS’s proposed extra capital requirement. The government is seeking roughly $20 billion of additional capital to protect the Swiss entity from losses in foreign subsidiaries. Letting UBS meet part of that demand with AT1 instead of common equity could lower its funding cost. UBS’s outstanding AT1 accounts for about 7% of the $286 billion European market, giving the proposal significance beyond one bank.

The committee tied that flexibility to earlier loss absorption. If UBS fell below its minimum common-equity capital requirement, the proposed rules would stop dividends, share buybacks and AT1 coupons and reduce the bonus pool. The Finance Ministry has questioned whether AT1 can absorb losses as reliably as common equity in a crisis. Social Democrats criticized the committee’s decision, and the lower house could reverse its concessions. The next vote is expected in the upper house’s Sept. 14-Oct. 2 session; the legislative process is due to continue at least into next year.

Asian data-center financing brought a capacity constraint into the same credit conversation. Loans to the sector have reached nearly $29 billion since the start of 2025, including a record $15 billion so far this year, 27% above the comparable 2025 period. Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers is discussing an expansion of an existing facility to as much as $7 billion, which would be the region’s largest data-center debt financing. Barclays’ Andrew Ashman said banks with heavy sector exposure are becoming more selective, favoring familiar borrowers or transactions with higher returns.

Some lenders are looking to distribute existing exposure. Crédit Agricole sought to sell part of a Hong Kong data-center loan, while Morgan Stanley explored a significant risk transfer to hedge its position. Barclays’ Richard Satchwell said asset-backed securities and project bonds could help recycle bank capital into longer-term markets. That route would increase lending capacity while putting more of the projects’ construction and operating risk before bond investors. Nvidia’s announced $3.5 billion investment in Taiwan’s MediaTek through convertible bonds, its largest direct investment outside the US, shows strategic technology capital still moving even as the banks financing physical capacity report tighter limits.

## Forward Market Significance

The next US releases will test whether Monday’s long-end selloff is reinforced by activity and inflation evidence. On Sept. 1, the final S&P Global manufacturing index is due at 9:45 a.m. New York time; consensus is 53.2 after 53.9 previously. The ISM manufacturing index follows at 10 a.m., with consensus at 55.2 after 55.6. Its orders, employment and prices components matter together: resilient production with firmer input costs would strengthen the case that energy pressure is arriving in an economy able to sustain it.

July JOLTS job openings and construction spending are also due at 10 a.m. Vacancies are expected at 7.3 million after 7.359 million, updating labor-demand breadth ahead of Friday’s payrolls report. Construction spending is expected to be unchanged after a 0.1% decline, giving another reading on demand sensitive to high borrowing costs. Economists expect August payrolls to rise 55,000 after July’s unexpected decline, with unemployment holding at 4.1%. A result near that profile would leave the Fed’s inflation assessment central; a materially weaker labor reading would make another September hold easier to defend.

Consumer prices on Sept. 11 are the more direct test of Warsh’s demand for clearer progress toward 2% before the Fed meets on Sept. 16. The question for bonds is whether September’s decision validates the tightening premium already embedded at shorter maturities or leaves longer investors assessing credibility and inflation risk without an increase. The path of oil through Hormuz matters alongside those releases because another sustained energy rise could change the price outlook between them.

Japan’s 10-year auction result is due Tuesday at 12:35 p.m. Tokyo time. Demand near a 3% yield, measured against the previous sale’s 2.56 bid-to-cover ratio, will show whether domestic buyers are prepared to absorb duration before the BOJ’s Sept. 17-18 meeting. A 30-year auction Thursday will separately test the super-long sector. Germany’s inflation mix now puts attention on the ECB’s Sept. 10 decision and on subsequent evidence of wage or services pass-through. New Zealand’s central bank is expected by all 21 economists surveyed to raise its Official Cash Rate 25 basis points to 2.75% on Wednesday; its statement will matter for the pace of further increases after inflation reached 4.1% even as unemployment rose to 5.6%.

Financing decisions offer more specific tests than broad risk appetite. Colombia’s coming auctions will show the concession needed to place more local debt, while Gómez’s meetings in the week of Sept. 7 may clarify the balance among bonds and multilateral funding. California lawmakers’ Tuesday vote will establish the wildfire-liability terms facing PG&E and Edison. CDK must bring remaining lenders into its exchange on the agreed priority terms, and UBS’s autumn parliamentary vote will determine whether the proposed AT1 compromise advances. For DayOne, final size, pricing and lender participation will show how much additional data-center exposure Asian banks can carry or distribute.
